families.comment: // Slot indices select one bit from each complete u64 word.
families.evidence: Masked search must return the same top-k set as an unmasked search filtered afterward.
prompts: Repair masked vector search so the frozen allowlist parity test passes. Choose one offered patch.
The top-k result must contain only permitted vector slots and match post-hoc filtering. The exact regression test currently fails; choose the patch that restores the packed-mask contract.

families.comment: // Remove the external ID before it can be reinserted.
families.evidence: After removal, the external ID must be absent so a replacement vector can reuse it.
prompts: Repair the stable-ID removal path. The frozen remove-and-readd test fails on this snapshot; choose the patch that makes the ID reusable.
A deleted external ID should no longer be reported as present, and a new vector must be allowed to reuse it. Select the offered implementation that satisfies the exact test.

families.comment: // The moved vector now occupies the vacated slot.
families.evidence: After swap-and-pop, every surviving external ID must continue to resolve to its vector.
prompts: Repair the ID-to-slot update after removing vectors from mixed positions. Choose the patch that keeps the frozen survivor search test passing.
A swap removal moves the last vector into the deleted vector's slot. Later removals and self-queries must still agree about each external ID; select the patch that restores that invariant.

families.comment: // This seed is part of the persisted v5 encoding contract.
families.evidence: The frozen v5 encoder must preserve its pinned deterministic rotation bytes.
prompts: Restore the v5 deterministic rotation contract. The frozen golden-byte test fails; choose the patch that preserves existing encoded data.
Changing the rotation stream changes persisted vector bytes. Use the exact test output and offered changes to select the patch that restores the recorded v5 format.

families.comment: // Preserve the caller's requested matching mode.
families.evidence: Case-insensitive mode must match the same pattern against an all-lowercase path.
prompts: Repair the case-insensitive glob option. The frozen mixed-case matching test fails; choose the patch that honors the requested mode.
A caller enables case-insensitive matching for a mixed-case pattern. Select the patch that makes the lowercase candidate match in the exact regression test.

families.comment: // Keep path separators literal when the option is enabled.
families.evidence: With literal separators enabled, a single-character wildcard must not consume a path separator.
prompts: Repair literal-separator matching for glob patterns. The exact separator test fails; choose the patch that preserves the requested path boundary.
When this option is enabled, `?` must not cross a path separator. Select the offered patch that makes the frozen negative-match test pass.

families.comment: // A middle `**/` spans zero or more whole directories.
families.evidence: A middle `**/` component must compile to the zero-or-more whole-directory regex, including a zero-directory match.
prompts: Repair the token selected for a middle `**/` component. The frozen regex contract test fails; choose the patch that preserves zero-or-more whole-directory semantics.
The middle recursive wildcard must allow zero directories or any number of whole directories. Select the patch that restores the exact compiled-regex contract.

families.comment: // Git ignores a UTF-8 BOM only at the start of the ignore file.
families.evidence: A UTF-8 BOM at the start of a .gitignore file must not become part of its first pattern.
prompts: Repair parsing of a .gitignore file that begins with a UTF-8 BOM. The frozen test cannot match its first rule; choose the patch that handles the file prefix.
Git-compatible parsing strips the BOM from the first line so that the rule still applies. Select the offered patch that makes the exact ignored-path check pass.
